The host term 'natural infection' is inferred from smear-positive dogs and is not stated in the abstract. Species are given as B. canis or B. gibsoni, unspecified, because the abstract says the disease in India is caused by either and diagnosis was by smear only.

verification_notes: Read the packet, the screening criteria, the guide and the full text (JATS XML converted to Markdown, quality ok, no flags). No web lookups were needed. The OpenAlex duplicate (W2768975266) is the same paper, listed under Annals of Parasitology with 'central Poland' in the title and year-only date; the PubMed record title and day-precision dates were kept. The abstract says co-infected dogs had more severe anaemia, but in Table 1 the erythrocyte, haemoglobin and haematocrit differences were not significant; only thrombocytes (P = 0.001), leukocytes (P = 0.007) and ALP (P = 0.007) were. The full text says 16 of 36 healthy-dog D. repens amplicons and 30 co-infection amplicons were sequenced, with GenBank accessions cited (KF494237, KM205374, EU622793, KT272401) that are existing sequences, not new deposits. Cats were surveyed for D. repens only, so host is given as dogs. The B. canis-only group is small (n = 5 for both haematology and biochemistry).

decision_reason: The paper is a methodical-guidelines article, but it reports haematology and biochemistry of dogs with severe babesiosis (anaemia, thrombocytopenia, leukocytosis, raised bilirubin, urea and creatinine, lower glucose) against milder cases, plus parasitaemia by age and season. This is a descriptive clinicopathological profile in natural infection, which the criteria include even though the paper also covers prevalence, treatment and tick control.

decision_reason: Case report with a mechanistic observation relevant to canine babesiosis anaemia: in a dog with numerous intraerythrocytic large Babesia and nonregenerative anaemia, polymethine-dye analysers (Sysmex XT-2000iV, ProCyte) gave a spurious automated reticulocyte count and scattergram cluster that the LaserCyte (new methylene blue) did not. This is distinct from a routine diagnosis and treatment case; decided on the abstract only.
